transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Got it, Sofia — you saw the ad about “missed calls,” and that’s been hitting you. What’s happening on your end when those calls come in—are you missing new buyer/seller leads, current clients, or after-hours stuff?
User: All of that! New leads, current clients — it’s a whirlwind, you know? I can't keep up!
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — that “whirlwind” feeling is real. When a call does go unanswered, do they usually leave a voicemail, or do they just call the next agent?
User: Voicemails? Sometimes. But they often just call the next agent! It's chaos. I need a solution.
Agent: Makes sense — if they’re calling the next agent, that’s business walking out the door. Roughly how many calls a week do you think are hitting voicemail or going unanswered?
User: I don't track that... maybe 25? Or 30? It's a mess!
Agent: Got it — let’s call it 30 a week for a clean number. Of those missed calls, what percent do you think would turn into an appointment if you actually answered—like 25%, 50%?
User: I mean, 25% would definitely book if I answered. Maybe more. Yes, tell me more about your service!
Agent: Got it — 25% is helpful. What’s an average commission or revenue per deal for you (ballpark), so I can do the quick math?
User: Oh, it varies, but around $10K per deal. So, missing calls really hits hard!
Agent: Yeah — with your numbers, that’s roughly **$324,700/month** in revenue slipping away from missed calls. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—I'll show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Actually, tomorrow works! But make sure to re-confirm the time because I changed the day.
Agent: Got it — tomorrow works, and we’ll re-confirm the time. What time zone are you in—Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Oh, I'm in Mountain — wait, no, Central! Yes, Central time for sure.
Agent: Perfect — Central time. What’s your last name?
User: Oh, it's Ramirez. So, what time tomorrow can we do this call? I need to lock it in!
Agent: Got it, Sofia Ramirez. And—quick check— is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the SMS confirmation?
User: Yes, this number is perfect for SMS. Can we confirm the exact time for tomorrow's call again?
Agent: Got it — we’ll use this number for the SMS confirmation. What time tomorrow works best for you (Central time)?
User: Let's do 10 AM Central. Can you confirm that time for me again? Just to be sure!
Agent: Yep — **10:00 AM Central tomorrow (Friday, Aug 28)** is available; is that the one you want me to put you down for?
User: Yes, please! Book me for 10 AM Central tomorrow. Can't wait! Remind me again in the morning, okay?
Agent: Quick thing - what's the best number to reach you on?
User: Sure, reach me at 555-123-4567. That's my direct line for everything.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: I’m getting an error with the calendar because it’s flagging the phone number as invalid. What’s the best mobile number for SMS if it’s different from 555-123-4567?
User: Great, thanks! Just let me know when it's all set. Looking forward to finally getting this sorted!
Agent: I hear you — the calendar won’t let me finalize it until we use a valid mobile number for SMS. What’s the best mobile number for you, including the area code?
User: Oh, of course! Use 713-555-9876. That's my mobile, with the area code and all.
Agent: Perfect — give me one moment while I lock in 10:00 AM Central tomorrow.
Agent: I’m seeing a conflict at **10:00 AM Central**—it’s showing as no longer available or already booked. Do you want **10:45 AM Central** instead?
User: Awesome, thanks! Looking forward to it. Please remind me again in the morning. Let's get this sorted!
Agent: I’m excited to get this sorted too — I just can’t confirm anything yet because **10:00 AM** conflicted. Do you want **10:45 AM Central tomorrow**?
User: 10:45 AM Central tomorrow works for me! Please confirm that slot, and we’re good to go. Thanks!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: I can book **10:45 AM Central tomorrow**, but I need to use your **mobile** for SMS—should I use **713-555-9876**?
User: Perfect, thanks! Once confirmed, just let me know. Can't wait to finally tackle these missed calls!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: I’m getting a conflict on **10:45 AM Central** too, so I can’t lock that one in. Do you want **11:30 AM Central tomorrow** instead?
User: Sure, take your time! Just let me know when it's confirmed. I'm excited to get started.
Agent: I hear you — I just can’t confirm it until we pick an open time. Do you want **11:30 AM Central tomorrow**?
User: Yes, 11:30 AM Central tomorrow works. Please confirm that slot, and we're all set. Excited to start!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: I’m still getting a calendar conflict at **11:30 AM Central**, so it won’t let me confirm that slot. Do you want to try **12:15 PM Central tomorrow**?
User: Great, I'll wait. Just let me know once it's set. I'm eager to get this sorted!
Agent: I hear you — I just can’t lock anything in until we pick an open time. Do you want **12:15 PM Central tomorrow**?
User: Yes, 12:15 PM Central tomorrow works. Please confirm that slot for me. Looking forward to it!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Sofia — you’re booked for **12:15 PM Central tomorrow** with Jay, and you’ll receive an **SMS text** with the confirmation details (you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if needed). Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, take your time! Just let me know once it's all confirmed. Excited to get started!
Agent: All set, Sofia — it’s confirmed, and you’ll get that SMS with the details shortly. Really glad you called; Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day — bye!
